\section[usiru]{\kn{ಉಸಿರು} (usiru) — breath}

\label{lesson:KA-C99-breath}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for alarm, then the Kannada for peace of mind.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಉಸಿರು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಉಸಿರು}} (\emph{usiru}) — \textquotedblleft{}breath\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ಉಸಿರು} \kn{ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ}} (\emph{usiru tegedukoḷḷi}) — \textquotedblleft{}take a breath\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\kn{ತೆಗೆದುಕೊ}}, \textquotedblleft{}take\textquotedblright{}, as in \textbf{\kn{ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ} \kn{ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What the body does all day.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{usiru}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{usiru}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{usiru tegedukoḷḷi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for alarm, then the Kannada for peace of mind, then say \emph{usiru} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಉಸಿರು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Breath\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[carma]{\kn{ಚರ್ಮ} (carma) — skin}

\label{lesson:KA-C99-skin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for peace of mind, then the Kannada for breath.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಚರ್ಮ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಚರ್ಮ}} (\emph{carma}) — \textquotedblleft{}skin\textquotedblright{}. The \textbf{\kn{ರ್}} sits on top of \textbf{\kn{ಮ}} as a small hook.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The body's cover.
\end{grammarlens}

\textbf{\kn{ರಕ್ತ}} (\emph{rakta}) — \textquotedblleft{}blood\textquotedblright{}. The \textbf{\kn{ಕ್ತ}} is \emph{k} and \emph{t} stacked into one.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A word for the doctor and the hospital.

\section[hoṭṭenōvu]{\kn{ಹೊಟ್ಟೆನೋವು} (hoṭṭenōvu) — a stomach ache}

\label{lesson:KA-C99-stomachache}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for skin, then the Kannada for blood.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಹೊಟ್ಟೆನೋವು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಹೊಟ್ಟೆನೋವು}} (\emph{hoṭṭenōvu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a stomach ache\textquotedblright{}, built exactly like \textbf{\kn{ತಲೆನೋವು}}: \textbf{\kn{ಹೊಟ್ಟೆ}} (\emph{hoṭṭe}), \textquotedblleft{}stomach\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\kn{ನೋವು}}, \textquotedblleft{}pain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The pattern of headache, used again.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hoṭṭenōvu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hoṭṭenōvu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nanage hoṭṭenōvu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for skin, then the Kannada for blood, then say \emph{hoṭṭenōvu} again

\section[tūka]{\kn{ತೂಕ} (tūka) — weight}

\label{lesson:KA-C99-weight}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for blood, then the Kannada for a stomach ache.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತೂಕ}}
\textbf{\kn{ತೂಕ}} (\emph{tūka}) — \textquotedblleft{}weight\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನಿಮ್ಮ} \kn{ತೂಕ} \kn{ಎಷ್ಟು}?} (\emph{nimma tūka eṣṭu?}) — \textquotedblleft{}what is your weight?\textquotedblright{}, a doctor's question, with \textbf{\kn{ಎಷ್ಟು}}, \textquotedblleft{}how much\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A number the doctor asks for.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tūka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tūka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{nimma tūka eṣṭu?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for blood, then the Kannada for a stomach ache, then say \emph{tūka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತೂಕ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Weight\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
